pr_title: lib: utils: json: fix floating point encode and decode
pr_body:
Add support for float and double floating types as primitives.

Fixes #59412
Signed-off-by: Eric Holmberg <eric.holmberg@northriversystems.co.nz>

issue_context.title: Json Floating Point Encoding
issue_context.body:
Hey, 

To facilitate the encoding of float numbers, developers need to store fields of type 'struct json_obj_token' in their structures instead of directly using float variables. However, this approach can be inconvenient, especially when dealing with multiple float variables within the struct. In such cases, developers are required to maintain temporary auxiliary char buffers for each float variable, converting the float values to strings. Additionally, if there is a requirement to process these values, they can be utilized directly as float numbers without any conversion from 'struct json_obj_token' to float. Consequently, it is advisable to modify the function name from "float_ascii_encode" to "float_encode," which invokes the "snprintk" function with the format "%f" and apparently another changes required.
comments: Was anything done on this? I believe this is something that is indeed missing.

Hey, 

you can apply the patch I've created—it hasn't been upstreamed.
[json_float_support.patch](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/14599205/json_float_support.patch)
Thanks, I was also thinking along the same lines.
Would love to see this fix cleaned up and merged and also fixes on the decode side.  Should changes be made to add support for doubles as well?

Hi @EricNRS, this requires a significant change, and I'm currently swamped with work. I've implemented a temporary local fix for now. If you have the time to take care of it, that would be great. I believe many people are eagerly waiting for this enhancement.
@ofirshe I'm swamped as well.  I pulled in your temporary fix (much appreciated) to kick the can down the road a bit further.
Needed decode support, so pushed through getting support for float and double into the library.  Will push the fix in a few minutes.
Also did a fix to allow using the JSON library from C++ for those brave souls:  https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/86692
I have closed https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/86800.  Please use https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/86956 as the fix for this issue.  It is ready for final review.

review_comments:
The buffer seems quite huge, I think it is sufficient to have 26 chars.
Sign + [0.] + digits + 'e+xxx' + '\0'
Indeed, 128 bytes is a bit large.  I will fix that.
Buffer size could be smaller, see comment on double_encode.

To keep the previous float handling, you could use an additional token 'JSON_TOK_OPAQUE_FLOAT' that uses the previous implementation (e.g. _float_ascii_encode_ function).  Hence, the old parsing style would still be available and clients would only need to change the float token name, e.g. in _lwm2m_rw_json.c_ rename JSON_TOK_FLOAT to JSON_TOK_OPAQUE_FLOAT.

I like that idea.

We still have users of this library that will need to change their code as well.  Guess I need to figure out how to add items to the migration guide - should I include the edits to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/doc/releases/migration-guide-4.2.rst in this commit?
